title: The Rescued Girl Is Received as the Khalsa’s Daughter

blocks.text: After the tyrant's death, attention turns from punishment to restoration. The rescued Brahmin girl is questioned with care, acknowledged as a victim of coercion rather than disgrace, and publicly embraced as the daughter of the Khalsa Panth.

That declaration immediately creates social obligation. The Singhs resolve to unite her with her in-laws, send messengers to her in-laws, and begin organizing communal support so that her return will be marked by dignity rather than stigma.
The page is therefore as important for social repair as for martial justice. A rescue is not considered complete until the community also rebuilds the injured woman's standing, security, and future.
